top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is one sharp idea (vanishing differential light shift with many atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime) realized to about 10^-18 and reproduced across independent laboratories. The two-person allocation of Katori (concept) and Ye (record performance and many-body regime) is clean, and the citation can state the distinction from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. Magic-angle graphene (P002) is a strong, productive discovery and my second choice, but its allocation and the interpretation of its correlated phases are less settled, and a prize is still preferable to no award.
